geo-mat.s: On a hill above Tbilisi stands a huge silver statue of a woman. She is called Mother of Georgia. In one hand she holds a cup. In the other she holds a sword. The cup is to welcome people who come in peace. The sword is to keep the home safe from people who come to do harm. The statue tells us about the Georgians. They love guests, but they know how to stand up for themselves.
a: An umbrella and an ice cream
A fishing rod and a bucket

geo-bukvy.s: Georgian letters do not look like any other letters. They are round and curly, like little rings and snails. The Georgian alphabet has thirty-three letters. Sentences do not start with a capital letter. And there is a funny mix-up in the Georgian language. The word “mama” means Dad, and Mum is called “deda”.

geo-pesnya.s: Georgians love to sing in a choir with many voices. One voice sings the tune. The others sing higher and lower. The voices weave together like threads in a pattern. This kind of singing is counted as a treasure of the whole world. In 1977 an old song called “Chakrulo” was put on a golden record. It was sent into space on a spacecraft called Voyager. It is still flying among the stars.

geo-hachapuri.s: Khachapuri is a Georgian bread with cheese. Adjarian khachapuri looks like a little boat. The edges curl up. Inside there is hot, stretchy cheese. An egg is cracked on top, with a piece of butter. You break off the crispy edge and dip it in the middle. For pudding there is churchkhela. It is nuts on a string, covered in thick grape juice.

geo-kazbek.s: In the north of Georgia are the high Caucasus mountains. One of the most beautiful is Kazbek. Snow and ice lie on it all year round, even in hot summer. In Georgian, the name of this mountain means “icy peak”. Below Kazbek, on a high green hill, stands the old Gergeti church. Visitors walk up to it.

geo-mtskheta.s: Mtskheta is one of the oldest cities in Georgia. Long ago, the capital of the country was here. Two rivers, the Aragvi and the Kura, meet here. You can often see that their water is a different colour. On the mountain above them stands the ancient Jvari Monastery. In the town there is the great Svetitskhoveli Cathedral. The poet Lermontov wrote about these rivers: “Hugging like two sisters, the streams of the Aragvi and the Kura.”

geo-batumi.s: Batumi is on the shore of the Black Sea. A long path with palm trees runs along the sea. The beach here is not sandy. It is made of smooth pebbles. Every evening, two huge metal figures by the sea come to life. They are a young man and a young woman. They slowly move towards each other. They meet and pass through each other. It looks like magic!

arm-ararat.s: On a clear day, you can see the huge Mount Ararat from Yerevan. It has two tops: Greater Ararat and Lesser Ararat. The bigger one has snow on it all year round, sparkling in the sun. An old story says that after the Great Flood, Noah's Ark landed on this mountain with all the animals. Armenians love Ararat very much. They often paint it in pictures.
a: None, it is as flat as a pancake

arm-tuf.s: Yerevan is called the pink city. Many houses here are built of tuff. Tuff is a stone made from the ash of very old volcanoes. It can be pink, orange and even lilac. It is soft and easy to carve, so people carve patterns on it. In the evening, when the sun goes down, the walls glow with a warm pink light.

arm-bukvy.s: More than fifteen hundred years ago, the Armenians did not have their own letters. Then a wise monk called Mesrop Mashtots made up the Armenian alphabet. It has thirty-six letters. Since then, Armenians have written with their own letters, with hooks and tails. On the side of Mount Aragats there are big stone Armenian letters. They are almost as tall as a person. You can walk among them as if in a stone forest.

arm-matenadaran.s: In Yerevan there is a place called the Matenadaran. In Armenian this means “a place to keep books”. Thousands of old books are kept here. They were written by hand and have bright pictures in them. The biggest book weighs more than a five-year-old child. The smallest one fits easily on your hand. At the door stands a statue of Mesrop Mashtots, who made up the Armenian letters.

arm-abrikos.s: Apricots have grown in Armenia for a very long time. Long ago, people in Europe thought apricots came from Armenia. So scientists gave the apricot a Latin name that means “Armenian plum”. In summer the markets have mountains of apricots, sweet and orange like little suns. People make the duduk from apricot wood. It is an Armenian pipe with a soft, singing voice.

arm-lavash.s: Armenian lavash is as thin as a sheet of paper. It is baked in a tonir. A tonir is a round clay oven in the ground. The women roll out the dough and stretch it. Then they neatly stick it onto the hot wall of the oven. Lavash bakes very quickly. Dry lavash stays good for a very long time. To make it soft again, you sprinkle it with water.
a: In a tonir, an oven in the ground

arm-sevan.s: Lake Sevan is a huge lake high in the mountains of Armenia. It is the biggest lake in Armenia and in the whole Caucasus. The water is blue and cool, even in summer. On the shore stand the old churches of Sevanavank monastery. They used to be on an island. Then the water in the lake went down. The island became a peninsula, which is land with water on three sides. Now you can walk to the monastery.

arm-garni.s: Almost two thousand years ago, people built the Garni temple in the mountains of Armenia. It looks like an ancient Greek temple. It has twenty-four columns all round it. People think the temple was made for the sun god. One day an earthquake knocked it down. Then scientists put it back together from the old stones. In the deep valley below the temple stand stone pillars. They look like the pipes of a huge organ. They are called the “Symphony of Stones”.

arm-shahmaty.s: Armenians love chess very much. An Armenian chess player called Tigran Petrosian was world champion. In 2011, Armenia was one of the first countries in the world to make chess a school lesson for everyone. From the second year, children learn how the knight moves. They learn to give checkmate. They learn to think a few moves ahead. In these lessons they learn not to hurry and to think carefully about every step.
a: Only when they are very old

arm-kaskad.s: In the middle of Yerevan, a huge pale staircase called the Cascade climbs up the hill. It has more than five hundred steps. Fountains bubble between the steps, and funny statues stand around. At the bottom, for example, sits a big fat cat made of bronze. If you get tired, you can go up inside the Cascade on an escalator. From the very top you can see all of Yerevan. On a clear day you can see Mount Ararat too.

srb-kalemegdan.s: In Serbian, Belgrade means “white city”. On the high river bank above it stands the old Kalemegdan fortress. From its walls you can see the River Sava flowing into the wide Danube. Around the fortress there is a big park. Families go for walks there, and children play. And right inside the fortress there is a zoo!

srb-tesla.s: Nikola Tesla was born in 1856 in the little village of Smiljan. He grew up to be a great inventor. His inventions helped bring electricity to homes all over the world. In Belgrade there is a museum about Nikola Tesla. There they switch on a huge coil. The lamp in a visitor's hand lights up all by itself, with no wires or batteries!
a: It lights up by itself, without wires
It flies out of the window

srb-sava.s: On a hill in Belgrade stands the huge white Temple of Saint Sava. It is one of the biggest Orthodox churches in the world. Go inside and look up. You will see a round roof that shines with golden mosaic. In Serbia, people say Saint Sava was the first teacher and looks after schools. So on the twenty-seventh of January, his day, all Serbian schools have a party.

srb-slivy.s: Lots and lots of plums grow in Serbia. They are one of the country's favourite fruits. At the end of summer, people cook thick plum jam called pekmez. They cook it for many hours in a big pot over a fire. They stir it with a long wooden paddle. People also bake plum pies. They make knedle too. These are balls of potato dough with a whole plum inside.

srb-guca.s: Every year in August, the little town of Guča in Serbia fills with music. Trumpet bands come from all over Serbia and from other countries. Trumpets and drums play loudly on every street. People hold hands and dance in a circle. The dance is called the kolo. The first festival like this was in 1961. Only four bands played in it then.

srb-djavolja.s: In the south of Serbia there is a place with a scary name: Devil's Town. But there is nothing to be afraid of. It is just stone pillars! There are more than two hundred of them. Many have a stone on top, like a hat. For hundreds of years, the rain washed away the soft earth around the pillars. The stone on top kept the earth under it safe, like an umbrella. That is how these amazing pillars in hats grew.
a: The stone on top, like an umbrella

srb-monastyri.s: Old monasteries are hidden in the green valleys of Serbia. One of the most famous is Studenica. Its main church was built of white marble more than eight hundred years ago. Inside, the walls are painted with frescoes. A fresco is a picture painted onto a wall while it is still wet. In the Mileševa monastery there is a famous fresco called the “White Angel”. It shows an angel in shining white robes.

srb-dunaj.s: The Danube flows through ten countries. No other river in the world flows through more. In the east of Serbia it winds between high cliffs, in a deep valley called the Iron Gates. Here the river becomes narrow and very deep. At the start of the valley stands the old Golubac fortress with its tall towers. On the rock above the water you can see words that the ancient Romans cut into it almost two thousand years ago.

srb-azbuka.s: The Serbian alphabet has thirty letters. Each letter is always read the same way. A wise man called Vuk Karadžić put the alphabet in order. His main rule is: “Write as you speak, and read as it is written.” The alphabet has some letters that Russian does not have. One sounds like “lj” and another like “nj”. Serbian children learn two alphabets, first Cyrillic, then Latin.
a: To write only with your foot

srb-djokovic.s: The famous tennis player Novak Djokovic was born in Belgrade. He first picked up a racket when he was four years old. He has won the biggest tennis competitions in the world many times. He became an Olympic champion too. Serbia loves basketball as well. Serbian basketball players play in the very best teams in the world.
a: He was born with a racket in his hand
